external_entities.name: Member
external_entities.description: A person who uses the loyalty platform, collects points, spends them on gift cards, and connects partner apps.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.
external_entities.notes: Individual members are outside the system's control; the text does not separately place members in a zone.

external_entities.name: Member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone on which the mobile app and its refresh token reside.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.
external_entities.notes: The text refers to members' phones in the plural.

external_entities.name: Partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers
external_entities.notes: Partner apps are external systems operated by other companies.

external_entities.name: Browser
external_entities.description: The browser used by a member to sign in to the authorization server and approve consent.
external_entities.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where the browser runs.

processes.name: Mobile app
processes.description: The mobile application through which members sign in, obtain tokens, call the rewards API, and manage partner connections.
processes.notes: The text does not state the mobile app's technology.

processes.name: Authorization server
processes.description: The server that authenticates members, handles authorization code flows and consent, and issues access and refresh tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: The authorization server also signs tokens for the support console.

processes.name: Rewards API
processes.description: The API called by the mobile app and partner apps to read and write loyalty points data.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: The API is served on the same public hostname as the support console.

processes.name: Support console
processes.description: A web application that closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: Identity database
data_stores.description: Database containing member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, consents, and account closure state.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_stores.notes: The database also contains authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.

data_stores.name: Points ledger
data_stores.description: Ledger containing every member's balance and every points transaction, including the client that made each change.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Store containing every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_stores.notes: The text does not state the log store's technology or protection.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs the member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: Nobody wrote down whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.
data_flows.data_description: authentication request and authorization code flow data

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with an access token.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.data_description: access token and loyalty rewards requests

data_flows.name: token request
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests to the authorization server using its client secret.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The client secret is sent in the request body.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret, authorization code, and token request data

data_flows.name: member sign-in
data_flows.description: The browser accesses the authorization server sign-in page for member authentication and consent.
data_flows.source_excerpt: signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

data_flows.name: show points
data_flows.description: A partner app uses the rewards API to show a member's points.
data_flows.source_excerpt: such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points
data_flows.notes: The text implies use of the partner API but does not specify the request details.

data_flows.name: disconnect partner
data_flows.description: The mobile app uses its settings screen to disconnect a partner app, causing its refresh token to be deleted from the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members can disconnect a partner app from the settings screen of the mobile app
data_flows.data_description: partner connection and refresh-token revocation request

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server reads and writes identity, authorization, token, consent, and account data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents

data_flows.name: read-write ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger

data_flows.name: write requests
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes received requests and headers to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: get access token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.

trust_boundaries.name: Own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The cloud account in which the platform components and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account

trust_boundaries.name: Member phones
trust_boundaries.description: The zone containing members' phones, apart from the platform's own cloud account.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: apart from the members' phones and the partner apps

trust_boundaries.name: Partner servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers owned and operated by other companies for their partner applications.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member personal information, passwords, tokens, and consents.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it contains member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens, and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member-linked balances and points transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because request headers may contain credentials or personal information.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request, headers included, is written to the API log store.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the rewards API is served on the same public hostname as the support console.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
